title: How to become a Pilates instructor in the UK: steps, cost and time
author: author-georgie
summary: Becoming a Pilates instructor in the UK takes a teacher training course, supported practice hours and exams. At The Pilates Programme in Altrincham the route is five in-person days, 80 practice hours and three exams, for £2,200. Most students teach their first paid class within three to four months.

image.alt: The Reformer studio at the Altrincham training centre

seo.title: How to Become a Pilates Instructor UK | The Pilates Programme
seo.description: The steps, cost and time it takes to qualify as a Pilates instructor in the UK, explained by a Manchester training provider.

body:
What does it take to become a Pilates instructor?

You need a teacher training course, practice hours and exams. The course teaches you the repertoire and how to teach it. The hours turn knowledge into skill. The exams show a studio you can be trusted with their clients.

Step 1: choose your first course

Most people start with Mat or Reformer. Mat is the fullest foundation and needs no equipment for practice. Reformer is what most boutique studios hire for. If you want both, a double booking saves £1,000.

Step 2: the in-person intensive

Our courses run as five in-person days in Altrincham. Before you arrive you complete the online Human Movement course so the practical days can focus on movement and teaching.

Step 3: practice hours

After the intensive you complete 30 observation hours, 25 personal study hours and 25 practice teaching hours. Spread over eight weeks that is around ten hours a week, which most students fit around a job.

Step 4: exams and your first class

Two multiple choice exams and a practical exam over Zoom, all included in the fee. Then you are ready to cover classes, apply for roles on our jobs board or start your own.

How much does it cost?

£2,200 for Mat, Reformer or Barre, with nothing extra for exams or your manual. Four monthly interest-free payments are available.

How long does it take?

Three to four months from booking to first paid class is typical. Longer is fine.

title: Mat or Reformer first? How to choose your first Pilates course
author: author-sarah
summary: Mat gives you the deepest foundation, works in any room and needs no equipment for practice hours. Reformer is the format most boutique studios are hiring for. Choose based on where you want to teach and whether you can practise on a Reformer. Many students book both and save £1,000.

image.alt: Reformers by the windows at the Altrincham training centre

seo.title: Mat or Reformer First? Choosing Your Pilates Course | The Pilates Programme
seo.description: How to decide between Mat and Reformer teacher training, from a Manchester provider that teaches both.

body:
Which should you train in first?

It depends on where you want to teach and what you can practise on. Here is how we help students decide.

Choose Mat first if

  • You want to teach anywhere: community halls, gyms, online, your own classes.
  • You do not have regular access to a Reformer for practice hours.
  • You want the fullest understanding of the method. Mat is where the repertoire comes from.

Choose Reformer first if

  • You want to work in boutique Reformer studios, which hire more teachers than any other format right now.
  • You can practise on a Reformer at a local studio, through hire at our centre, or at home.

Or do both

A double booking of any two of Mat, Reformer and Barre is £3,400, a saving of £1,000, with six interest-free payments. Many of our students qualify in both within six months.

Still unsure?

Take the 60-second course quiz on the Qualify hub. It asks four questions and recommends a route.

title: Completing your 80 practice hours: an 8-week plan
author: author-georgie
summary: The 80 practice hours after your intensive are 30 observation, 25 personal study and 25 practice teaching. Spread over eight weeks that is ten hours a week. This plan shows a realistic week, where to find classes to observe, and how to practise teaching before your exam.

image.alt: The seminar room at the Altrincham training centre

seo.title: Pilates Practice Hours: an 8-Week Plan | The Pilates Programme
seo.description: A week-by-week plan for the 80 practice hours between your Pilates teacher training intensive and your exams.

body:
Why the hours matter

The hours are the reason studios trust our graduates. Anyone can learn a sequence in a weekend. Teaching real bodies, watching experienced teachers and studying the theory is what makes you employable.

The three types of hours

  • 30 observation hours. Watch classes at a local studio, at our centre, or online through the video library.
  • 25 personal study hours. Your own practice, the manual and the online platform.
  • 25 practice teaching hours. Teach friends, family, fellow students or a studio that will have you.

A realistic week

Four hours of observation, three of study, three of teaching. Two evenings and a Saturday morning covers it.

Weeks 1 to 2

Observation heavy. Book onto classes and watch how teachers cue and manage a room.

Weeks 3 to 5

Start teaching short sections to friends. Keep observing. Begin exam revision.

Weeks 6 to 8

Teach full 45-minute classes. Hire studio space at the centre if you need a room and equipment. Book your practical exam.

Support

Your trainers are available throughout, and you can hire studio space and equipment at the Altrincham centre for practice.
